cities.name: Beijing
cities.tagline: The historic heart of China
cities.description: 3,000 years of history meets modern ambition. Walk the Great Wall, explore the Forbidden City, get lost in hutong alleys, then hit cutting-edge art districts. As the capital, Beijing gives you the densest cultural experience in one trip.
bestFor: First-time visitors wanting the classic China experience

cities.name: Shanghai
cities.tagline: The easiest first landing in China
cities.description: China's most international city. The Bund skyline, French Concession charm, world-class metro with English signs. You'll find more English speakers and fewer culture shocks here than anywhere else in mainland China.
bestFor: First-time visitors wanting the softest landing

cities.name: Guangzhou
cities.tagline: Cantonese food capital with a tropical soul
cities.description: The best-value tier-1 city in China. Incredible Cantonese food at budget prices, tropical parks, tree-lined islands, and a deep mercantile history. Warm winters make it a great escape during colder months.

cities.name: Shenzhen
cities.tagline: China's tech capital with surf beaches
cities.description: A futuristic city that didn't exist 40 years ago. Skyscrapers, tech HQs, theme parks, and surprisingly good beaches. Young, fast, and the most Mandarin-friendly city in the south. Great for tech-curious travelers and families.

cities.name: Chengdu
cities.tagline: Pandas, teahouses, and the good life
cities.description: Where China slows down. Mornings with giant pandas, afternoons in traditional teahouses, evenings eating Sichuan cuisine from fiery hotpot to subtle flavors. Relaxed pace, great food, gateway to Tibet and western Sichuan mountains.

cities.name: Chongqing
cities.tagline: The most dramatic city you will ever see
cities.description: A megacity built on mountains — trains run through buildings, streets stack vertically, night skyline reflects off the Yangtze. Capital of hotpot. Rewards adventurous travelers who want visual spectacle.

cities.name: Hangzhou
cities.tagline: Paradise on earth, just an hour from Shanghai
cities.description: Marco Polo called it the finest city in the world. West Lake, tea plantations, bamboo forests, and a thriving tech scene. Combines classical Chinese beauty with modern comfort. Perfect day trip or weekend from Shanghai.

cities.name: Nanjing
cities.tagline: Six dynasties, one unforgettable city
cities.description: Ancient capital with tree-lined boulevards, the imposing Ming city wall, Sun Yat-sen Mausoleum, and a darkly fascinating Republican-era history. Duck blood soup aside, the food scene is excellent and underrated.

cities.name: Suzhou
cities.tagline: Classical gardens and silk roads
cities.description: Venice of the East. UNESCO-listed classical gardens, ancient canals, and silk history. Close to Shanghai, making it an easy day trip or overnight. One of China's most beautiful small cities with surprisingly good modern infrastructure.

cities.name: Xi'an
cities.tagline: Walk among 2,000-year-old warriors
cities.description: Ancient Silk Road starting point, home to the Terracotta Warriors. Intact city walls you can bike on, the Muslim Quarter's unique street food paradise, and Tang Dynasty history in every corner. Compact enough for 2-3 days.
bestFor: Combining with Beijing on a two-city trip

cities.name: Wuhan
cities.tagline: The heart of central China
cities.description: Mega-city where the Yangtze and Han rivers meet. Famous for morning street breakfasts (hot dry noodles), cherry blossoms in spring, and Yellow Crane Tower. A transport hub that's growing fast as a destination in its own right.

cities.name: Changsha
cities.tagline: China's youth culture capital
cities.description: Buzzing nightlife, the spiciest food in China, and a young creative energy that's become legendary on Chinese social media. Hunan cuisine is fiercer than Sichuan. Not a first-trip city but unforgettable for food and nightlife.

cities.name: Zhengzhou
cities.tagline: Gateway to ancient China's heartland
cities.description: Transport hub and gateway to Shaolin Temple and the Longmen Grottoes. The city itself is modern and busy, but it's the best base for exploring Henan's deep ancient history, including the Yellow River and Song Dynasty ruins.

cities.name: Qingdao
cities.tagline: Beaches, beer, and Bavarian architecture
cities.description: Coastal city with German colonial architecture, China's most famous beer (Tsingtao), fresh seafood, and sandy beaches. Hosts an international beer festival every summer. Feels more European than any other Chinese city.

cities.name: Xiamen
cities.tagline: Island charm with a literary soul
cities.description: Subtropical island city with car-free Gulangyu Island, colonial architecture, and a relaxed seaside vibe. Famous for oolong tea, seafood noodles, and a slower pace. One of China's most livable cities and a favorite weekend escape.

cities.name: Kunming
cities.tagline: City of eternal spring
cities.description: Mild weather year-round, gateway to Yunnan's ethnic diversity and natural wonders. Stone Forest, flower markets, and a crossroads of Southeast Asian cultures. The best base for exploring Dali, Lijiang, and Shangri-La.

cities.name: Dali
cities.tagline: Lakeside bliss beneath snow-capped mountains
cities.description: Ancient town between Erhai Lake and Cangshan Mountain. Backpacker favorite with cobblestone streets, Bai minority culture, cycling routes, and a creative expat community. Feels like a dream for anyone escaping big-city stress.

cities.name: Lijiang
cities.tagline: UNESCO old town with Jade Dragon Snow Mountain backdrop
cities.description: 800-year-old cobblestone maze of canals, wooden bridges, and Naxi minority culture. Jade Dragon Snow Mountain towers above. Touristy in peak season, but the old town at dawn is pure magic. Gateway to Tiger Leaping Gorge.

cities.name: Guilin / Yangshuo
cities.tagline: China's most iconic natural landscape
cities.description: The karst mountains you've seen on Chinese paintings and postcards. Li River cruises between misty limestone peaks, cycling through Yangshuo rice paddies, climbing Xianggong Hill for sunrise. Best nature escape for first-time visitors.

cities.name: Zhangjiajie
cities.tagline: The mountains that inspired Avatar
cities.description: Towering sandstone pillars rising through mist, glass skywalks, and the world's longest cable car. The landscape that inspired Avatar's floating mountains. Intense nature experience — requires decent fitness for all the steps.

cities.name: Huangshan
cities.tagline: The mountain that defined Chinese art
cities.description: Yellow Mountain's granite peaks, twisted pines, and sea of clouds have inspired Chinese painters for centuries. Hot springs at the base, ancient villages nearby. The most beautiful mountain in China — worth the steep climb.

cities.name: Tianjin
cities.tagline: 30 minutes from Beijing, worlds apart
cities.description: Beijing's coastal neighbor with a distinct identity: former foreign concessions, the best jianbing (savory crepes) in China,相声 (cross-talk comedy), and a more laid-back northern lifestyle. Great half-day or overnight add-on.

cities.name: Harbin
cities.tagline: Russian winter wonderland in China
cities.description: Ice palaces, sub-zero festivals, Russian Orthodox churches, and Siberian tiger parks. The annual Ice and Snow Festival (January-February) is one of the world's most spectacular winter events. Coldest major city in China — bring serious layers.

cities.name: Shenyang
cities.tagline: Manchu imperial roots and industrial grit
cities.description: The Mukden Palace — a mini Forbidden City — and the 9.18 Historical Museum offer deep dives into Qing dynasty and modern history. Gritty northern charm, Korean-influenced food scene, and a gateway to North Korea border tours.

cities.name: Dalian
cities.tagline: Northern China's most beautiful coastal city
cities.description: Clean air, European-style squares, seafood feasts, and sandy beaches. Built by Russians and Japanese, Dalian feels more like a Mediterranean resort than a Chinese industrial city. Summer escape for northerners and a hidden gem for foreigners.

cities.name: Changchun
cities.tagline: Japan's lost imperial capital, now a winter sports hub
cities.description: Home to the Puppet Emperor's Palace — a bizarre remnant of Japan's Manchukuo state. Today it's China's film industry capital and has surprisingly good ski resorts nearby. Rime ice on trees in winter is otherworldly.

cities.name: Jinan
cities.tagline: City of springs and Confucian roots
cities.description: 72 natural springs bubble up through the city center — rare anywhere in the world. Gateway to Mount Tai (China's most sacred mountain) and Qufu (Confucius' hometown). Shandong cuisine is the root of northern Chinese cooking.

cities.name: Hefei
cities.tagline: Science city with Anhui charm
cities.description: China's fastest-growing research hub with quantum labs and AI centers. Base for exploring ancient Huizhou villages and Huangshan. Not a classic tourist city, but good for tech travelers and as a Huangshan staging point.

cities.name: Fuzhou
cities.tagline: Banyan trees, hot springs, and Fujian soul
cities.description: A green, laid-back capital with ancient banyan trees shading entire streets. Fujian cuisine is subtle and seafood-focused — Buddha Jumps Over the Wall is the famous local dish. Easy add-on before or after Xiamen. Hot springs abound.

cities.name: Nanning
cities.tagline: The greenest city in China, gateway to Southeast Asia
cities.description: Lush, tropical, and the most relaxed provincial capital in China. Famous for rice noodles and a gateway to the Vietnam border, Detian Waterfall, and Guangxi's karst countryside beyond Guilin. ASEAN expat hub with a multicultural food scene.

cities.name: Guiyang
cities.tagline: Mountain capital with sour-spicy soul
cities.description: Built among forested hills, Guiyang is the gateway to Guizhou's Miao and Dong minority villages, Huangguoshu Waterfall, and one of China's most underrated food scenes. Sour-spicy flavors you won't find anywhere else.

cities.name: Lanzhou
cities.tagline: The Yellow River and the world's best beef noodles
cities.description: The Yellow River cuts through the city center. Lanzhou hand-pulled beef noodles are legendary across China. Gateway to the Silk Road — Zhangye's rainbow mountains, Jiayuguan's Great Wall end, and Dunhuang's Mogao Caves.

cities.name: Dunhuang
cities.tagline: Buddhist art in the desert
cities.description: Mogao Caves — 1,000 years of Buddhist art carved into desert cliffs. Singing Sand Dunes, Crescent Moon Spring oasis, and Silk Road camel treks. Remote, otherworldly, and deeply moving. Worth the journey for anyone interested in Buddhism, art, or deserts.

cities.name: Urumqi
cities.tagline: The most Central Asian city in China
cities.description: Mosques, bazaars, lamb skewers, and Uyghur culture in a modern Chinese city. Gateway to Heavenly Lake and the vast Xinjiang landscapes. The food is unlike anything else in China — Central Asian grilled meats, hand-pulled noodles, and naan bread.

cities.name: Lhasa
cities.tagline: The roof of the world
cities.description: Potala Palace rising above the Tibetan plateau at 3,650 meters. Jokhang Temple, Barkhor Street pilgrims, and some of the most intense light and color anywhere on earth. Requires altitude preparation and permits — not a casual add-on.

cities.name: Xining
cities.tagline: High-plateau gateway to Qinghai Lake
cities.description: China's most underrated summer destination. Qinghai Lake — a vast turquoise inland sea — is nearby. Tibetan and Muslim culture blend in the markets. Cool summer temperatures when the rest of China is sweltering. Start of the Qinghai-Tibet railway.

cities.name: Yinchuan
cities.tagline: Desert lakes and Western Xia mysteries
cities.description: An oasis city where the Yellow River meets the desert. Western Xia Imperial Tombs — China's 'pyramids' — are nearby. Sand Lake is a surreal mix of desert dunes, reeds, and migratory birds. Ningxia wine region is China's best-kept secret.

cities.name: Hohhot
cities.tagline: Grasslands and Mongolian culture
cities.description: Gateway to Inner Mongolia's grasslands, where you can sleep in a yurt, ride horses, and eat whole roast lamb. Mongolian hotpot and milk tea are the local staples. The grasslands are best June through August — short but glorious summer.

cities.name: Taiyuan
cities.tagline: Ancient China above ground and below
cities.description: Gateway to Pingyao Ancient City and the Yungang Grottoes. Shanxi noodles are the best in northern China — knife-cut, hand-pulled, cat's ear. The province has more ancient buildings than anywhere else in China. Under-visited, over-delivers.

cities.name: Shijiazhuang
cities.tagline: Beijing's southern sibling with revolutionary roots
cities.description: Not a typical tourist city, but a good base for exploring Zhaozhou Bridge (world's oldest open-spandrel stone bridge), Zhengding ancient temples, and the Xibaipo revolutionary site. Easy 1-hour train from Beijing.
bestFor: Ancient bridge and temple day trips

cities.name: Nanchang
cities.tagline: Porcelain capital and Communist cradle
cities.description: 1927 Nanchang Uprising site and gateway to Jingdezhen — China's porcelain capital for 1,000 years. Poyang Lake (China's largest freshwater lake) is nearby for birdwatching. Tengwang Pavilion is one of China's four great towers.

cities.name: Haikou
cities.tagline: Tropical island capital with old-town soul
cities.description: Hainan's laid-back capital with Qilou arcade streets, volcanic parks, and coconut-lined beaches. Less resort-y than Sanya, more authentically Hainanese. Great winter escape and duty-free shopping destination. Hainan chicken rice originated nearby.

cities.name: Sanya
cities.tagline: China's Hawaii — palm trees and turquoise water
cities.description: The best tropical beach destination in China. Luxury resorts, clear water, diving, rainforest parks, and duty-free shopping. Popular with Russian tourists and Chinese honeymooners. Winter is peak season — book early and expect higher prices.

cities.name: Luoyang
cities.tagline: Peonies, grottoes, and 13 dynasties
cities.description: One of China's four great ancient capitals. Longmen Grottoes — thousands of Buddha carvings in limestone cliffs — are a UNESCO masterpiece. White Horse Temple is China's first Buddhist temple. April peony festival transforms the city.
bestFor: Day trip from Zhengzhou or Xi'an
